objectReview.reason: Retains diffusion as mixing caused by irregular molecular motion, microscope observation of insoluble suspended particles, random water-molecule impacts, the Brownian-motion name, thermal-motion evidence, Brown/British/1827, gamboge as an observation material, persistence while freely suspended, and a qualified temperature trend with viscosity. Observed particles are explicitly not individual molecules. Brown's plant-pollen wording and the non-priority clarification translate the already approved Chinese history; neither restores the source's universal first-observer claim nor invents a new one.

Retains kinetic explanation, incomplete cancellation over short times, particle and neighboring molecules in Figure 4, unequal left/right random impulses, greater relative pressure fluctuations on smaller force-bearing areas, a few-molecular-diameters scale, and the source's simplified force-jump picture. Crucially, unbiased averaging applies only to thermal random impulses in a uniform, no-flow, directionally equivalent medium; it is not a statement that total motion has no external-force or settling drift. No scale, force, size or speed is asserted to have been measured from the diagram.

Retains Einstein/1905 and the quantitative theory's evidential role without the source's absolute triumph rhetoric or a new exclusivity claim. Retains irregular molecular motion, the name thermal motion, its temperature relation, and its distinction from macroscopic mechanical motion. Preserves the approved correction that whole-body motion and internal thermal motion can coexist, rather than implying every constituent moves regularly.

flowParagraphReview.reason: Starts with diffusion and gives a concrete microscope observation; explicitly separates visible suspended particles from water molecules.
Defines Brownian motion through collisions, then attaches Brown's 1827/British history to the observation without priority inflation.
The priority caution is source-history clarification, not a new claim; gamboge remains a second insoluble-particle example. The pronoun him clearly refers to Brown.
Persistence is restricted to freely suspended particles; fixation, settling and solidification prevent a misleading never-stop free-motion claim.
Temperature comparison holds particle/medium conditions comparable and mentions viscosity as resistance; it is not an unconditional temperature-only law.
Introduces the microscopic explanation using short-time collision impulses, without claiming exact cancellation or sustained acceleration in one direction.
Identifies what Figure 4 represents and disclaims actual size/speed scales. This is a reading of the prose context, not a fresh image inspection.
Unequal instantaneous left/right effects are kept distinct from isotropic, uniform, no-macroscopic-flow averaging of thermal impulses.
Explicitly states that no average thermal directional bias neither means every impulse set cancels nor excludes external-force/settling drift.
Retains relative pressure fluctuations and the small-area molecular-diameter comparison with comparable conditions; no new numerical scale is supplied.
Retains the original collision-force picture as a simplified model rather than a measured or universal binary-valued liquid force.
Einstein's 1905 quantitative theory and measurable evidence are retained with cautious attribution, not an exclusive discovery claim.
Extends the mechanism to surrounding liquid or gas molecules while maintaining suspended-particle/molecule distinction.
Defines thermal motion and distinguishes it from whole-body position change with a temperature relation that is not overprecise.
Closes the actual conceptual distinction: internal thermal motion persists during macroscopic body motion, so regularity of all parts is not required.
